text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
AL-AHRAM

- The ministerial commitee for tourism development, at a four-hour meeting yesterday, took some important decisions designed to set the guidelines for developing tourism and allocating land in tourist areas.

- President Hosni Mubarak approved a number of military appointments. The new head of training is Staff Major-General Amr Khodeir, the commander of the western region is Staff Major-General Zaki Abdelghani Suleiman and the commander of the southern region is Staff Major-General Said Mohamed Nassef.

- At its next meeting the cabinet will discuss the debts of public-sector contracting companies, which vary from three to five billion pounds ($900 million to $1.5 billion) in the form of overdrafts from the commercial banks.
- Interior Minister Hassan el-Alfi told ruling party youth that the ministry is monitoring attempts by leading terrorists abroad to revive their organisations.
- Italy has reduced the premiums for insuring Italian exports to Egypt, on the grounds that exporting to Egypt has become low-risk.
AL-AKHBAR
- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzaouri said a tourism boom would come about by drawing up a new map of tourism investment.
- Cotton exports are worth 602 million pounds.
- Front-page editorial says "There is no difference between Israel and Iran when it comes to aggressiveness."
- Three Nile cruiseboats have run aground in the province of Minya and Beni Suef because the Nile is so low.
AL-GOMHURIA
- The Arab Affairs committee of the Advisory Council said it supported President Mubarak in his efforts for a just peace.
- Aberrahman Hafez has been named head of the Egyptian Radio and Television Union.
- A six-hour fire in a shop in Zagazig destroyed goods valued at three million pounds. There were no casualties.
- Alfi said that in local elections people should not be deceived by candidates who use religion as cover.
AL-WAFD
- Alfi reveals plan to cause chaos during the local elections.
$1 = 3.40 pounds
